primary_surface: About page + /app capture paths + podcast apps + Summary Mode + digest + wiki
script: I built ArticlePod for a problem I knew too well. I grew up around doctors and professors, so learning always mattered to me. Then life got busy. As an engineer, builder, and mom, I kept subscribing to newsletters, saving articles, opening PDFs, and leaving more than 50 tabs across devices. My browser was not a knowledge system. It was a very confident pile of good intentions. I wanted to stay current, but I kept stopping halfway through and rarely returning. ArticlePod is my attempt to turn that guilt pile into a habit. Paste a URL, upload a text-based PDF, or capture the page from Chrome. ArticlePod turns it into a private podcast episode that shows up in the podcast app you already use. One saved item, one episode. For lighter reading, Summary Mode gives you the recap first, and you can request audio later. For weekly catch-up, digests pull the throughline together. And over time, the personal wiki keeps the ideas, snippets, and sources connected, so learning does not disappear after one listen. This is not about replacing reading. It is about making the reading list effortless enough to finish. If you save thoughtful articles but struggle to get back to them, try ArticlePod with one article this week.

Now a URL, PDF, or Chrome capture can become a private podcast episode, a summary, a digest, and eventually part of a personal wiki. What would help you actually finish the things you save?
